children: European earnings revisions bucked a seasonal trend to strengthen ahead of the third-quarter earnings season, Citi strategists say. Companies on the continent have revised their earnings guidance upward in the pre-reporting period for the second consecutive quarter, only the sixth time this has happened over the past 25 years, the strategists say. The backdrop for European equities going into the third quarter earnings season is more constructive than usual, they say. Markets continue to price in upgrades to earnings-per-share growth forecasts over the next 12 months, they say, which could lift the bar for earnings beats to impress investors. The Stoxx Europe 600 falls 1.1% Monday, but remains up 7.7% for the year. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
